Two resistors $R$ and $2 R$ are connected in series with a battery. The ratio of power consumed by $R$ to that by $2 R$ is:
questions.s: In series, current (I) is the same. Power $P=I^{2} R . P \propto R$. So, $\frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\frac{R}{2 R}=\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: A galvanometer coil has a resistance of $15 \Omega$ and gives full-scale deflection for a current of 4 mA . To convert it to an ammeter of range 0 to 6 A , the shunt resistance required is approximately:
questions.s: $S=\frac{I_{g} G}{I-I_{g}}=\frac{\left(4 \times 10^{-3}\right) \times 15}{6-\left(4 \times 10^{-3}\right)} \approx \frac{0.06}{6}=0.01 \Omega$.

questions.q: For a Wheatstone bridge to be most sensitive, the resistances in all four arms should be:
questions.s: The sensitivity of a Wheatstone bridge is maximum when the bridge is nearly balanced and the resistances of all four arms are of a comparable magnitude.

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $100 \Omega$ gives full-scale deflection for a current of 1 mA . To convert it into a voltmeter of range 50 V , the required series resistance is:
questions.s: The required series resistance is $R=\frac{V}{I_{g}}-G=\frac{50 \mathrm{~V}}{1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~A}}-100 \Omega=50000 \Omega-100 \Omega=49900 \Omega$.

questions.q: The resistance of an ammeter is the equivalent resistance of:
o: The galvanometer and shunt resistance in series.
The galvanometer and shunt resistance in parallel.
questions.s: An ammeter is constructed by connecting a shunt resistor in parallel with the galvanometer. Its total resistance is the equivalent resistance of this parallel combination.

questions.q: To convert a galvanometer into an ammeter, one needs to connect:
questions.s: A low resistance shunt is connected in parallel to the galvanometer. This allows most of the current to bypass the galvanometer, enabling the measurement of a larger current.

questions.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, if the positions of the cell and the galvanometer are interchanged, the bridge will:
o: show a very high current in the galvanometer.
questions.s: The condition for a balanced Wheatstone bridge, $\frac{P}{Q}=\frac{R}{S}$, remains the same even if the battery and galvanometer are interchanged. The bridge remains balanced.

questions.q: The balancing length of a meter bridge is sensitive when the resistances in the two gaps are:
o: Of the same order of magnitude.
questions.s: The sensitivity of a meter bridge is highest when the balancing point is near the center of the wire (around 50 cm ). This occurs when the resistances in the two gaps are nearly equal.

questions.q: Two cells of EMFs $E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$ and internal resistances $r_{1}$ and $r_{2}$ are connected in parallel. The equivalent EMF of the combination is:
questions.s: The standard formula for the equivalent EMF of two cells connected in parallel is $E_{e q}=\frac{E_{1} / r_{1}+E_{2} / r_{2}}{1 / r_{1}+1 / r_{2}}=\frac{E_{1} r_{2}+E_{2} r_{1}}{r_{1}+r_{2}}$.

questions.q: A wire of resistance R is cut into 'n' equal parts. These parts are then connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of the combination will be:
questions.s: The resistance of each part is $R^{\prime}=R / n$. When 'n' such resistors are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance is $R_{e q}=\frac{R^{\prime}}{n}=\frac{R / n}{n}=\frac{R}{n^{2}}$.
questions.sub: Calculation of equivalent resistance of a circuit

questions.q: An ideal voltmeter has:
questions.s: An ideal voltmeter is connected in parallel and should not draw any current from the circuit to give an accurate reading of the potential difference. This requires its resistance to be infinite.

questions.q: A heater coil is cut into two equal parts and only one part is now used in the heater. With the same voltage supply, the heat produced will be:
questions.s: When the coil is cut in half, its resistance becomes $\mathrm{R} / 2$. Power $P= V^{2} / R$. The new power is $P^{\prime}=\frac{V^{2}}{R / 2}=2 \frac{V^{2}}{R}=2 P$. The heat produced will be doubled.

questions.q: In a balanced meter bridge, the resistance in the left gap is $2 \Omega$ and the resistance in the right gap is 3 $\Omega$. The balancing point from the left end is at:
questions.s: For a balanced meter bridge, $\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=\frac{l}{100-l} \cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{l}{100-l} \Rightarrow 2(100-l)=3 l \Rightarrow 200-2 l=3 l \Rightarrow 5 l=200 \Rightarrow l=40 \mathrm{~cm}$.

questions.q: The range of an ammeter can be increased by:
questions.s: From the formula $S=\frac{I_{g} G}{I-I_{g}}$, to increase the range I, the denominator ( $I-I_{g}$ ) must increase. For the equation to hold, the shunt resistance S must decrease. A smaller shunt bypasses more current.

questions.q: Kirchhoff's first law (junction rule) is a statement of conservation of:
questions.s: The junction rule states that the sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum of currents leaving it. This implies that no charge accumulates at the junction, thus it is a statement of the conservation of charge.

questions.q: The specific resistance of a conductor increases with:
questions.s: For a conductor, resistivity (specific resistance) increases with an increase in temperature due to more frequent collisions of electrons with the lattice ions. It is an intrinsic property and does not depend on length or area.
questions.sub: Temperature dependence of resistivity and resistance

questions.q: The deflection in a moving coil galvanometer is reduced from 50 divisions to 10 divisions when a shunt of $12 \Omega$ is connected. The resistance of the galvanometer is:
questions.s: Let the current for 50 divisions be I. Then the current for 10 divisions is $I_{g}=I / 5$. The current through the shunt is $I_{s}=I-I_{g}=I-I / 5=4 I / 5 . I_{g} G=I_{s} S \Rightarrow(I / 5) G=(4 I / 5)(12) \Rightarrow G=4 \times 12=48 \Omega$.

questions.q: A wire of resistance $12 \Omega$ is bent to form a circle. The equivalent resistance between two diametrically opposite points is:
questions.s: The wire is bent into a circle. Between two diametrically opposite points, there are two semicircular paths. The resistance of each path is $12 / 2=6 \Omega$. These two paths are in parallel. $R_{e q}=\frac{6 \times 6}{6+6}=\frac{36}{12}=3 \Omega$.
questions.sub: Calculation of equivalent resistance of a circuit

questions.q: In an RC circuit, the time constant is the time taken for the charge on the capacitor to reach approximately:
questions.s: The charge during charging is given by $Q(t)=Q_{\max }\left(1-e^{-t / \tau}\right)$. At $t=\tau$ (one time constant), the charge is $Q(\tau)=Q_{\max }\left(1-e^{-1}\right) \approx 0.632 Q_{\max }$. This is about $63 \%$ of the final maximum charge.

questions.q: Two electric bulbs are rated $25 \mathrm{~W}-220 \mathrm{~V}$ and $100 \mathrm{~W}-220 \mathrm{~V}$. If they are connected in series to a 220 V supply, which bulb will glow brighter?
o: Both will glow with the same brightness
questions.s: Resistance $R=V^{2} / P$. The 25 W bulb has higher resistance. In a series connection, the current (I) is the same through both. Power consumed is $P=I^{2} R$. The bulb with higher resistance ( 25 W bulb) will dissipate more power and glow brighter.

questions.q: The resistance of a wire is R . It is stretched uniformly so that its length becomes 'n' times the original length. The new resistance will be:
questions.s: When a wire is stretched, its volume remains constant. $V=A L$. If length becomes $n L$, the new area $A^{\prime}=A / n$. New resistance $R^{\prime}=\rho \frac{L^{\prime}}{A^{\prime}}=\rho \frac{n L}{A / n}= n^{2}\left(\rho \frac{L}{A}\right)=n^{2} R$.

questions.q: The magnetic flux linked with a coil of resistance $10 \Omega$ is given by $\phi=4 t^{2}-10 t+5$ (in SI units). The magnitude of the induced current in the coil at $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$ is:
questions.s: Induced emf $\mathcal{E}=-\frac{d \phi}{d t}=-(8 t-10)$. At $t=2 \mathrm{~s}, \mathcal{E}=-(8(2)-10)=-(16-10)=-6$ V . The magnitude is $|\mathcal{E}|=6 \mathrm{~V}$. The induced current is $I=\frac{|\mathcal{E}|}{R}=\frac{6 \mathrm{~V}}{10 \Omega}=0.6 \mathrm{~A}$.

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $100 \Omega$ requires 2 mA for full-scale deflection. The value of series resistance required to convert it into a voltmeter of range $0-10 \mathrm{~V}$ is_____ \[\left( {{\text{in}}\,\,\,\Omega } \right).\]
questions.s: The required series resistance is $R=\frac{V}{I_{g}}-G=\frac{10 \mathrm{~V}}{2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~A}}-100 \Omega=5000 \Omega-100 \Omega=4900 \Omega$.

questions.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, the four arms have resistances $P=10 \Omega, Q=30 \Omega, R=5 \Omega$, and S . The value of S is_____ \[\left( {{\text{in}}\,\,\,\Omega } \right).\]
questions.s: For the bridge to be balanced, the ratio of resistances must be equal: $\frac{P}{Q}=\frac{R}{S} \Rightarrow \frac{10}{30}=\frac{5}{S} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{3}=\frac{5}{S} \Rightarrow S=15 \Omega$.

questions.q: Three resistors of $4 \Omega, 6 \Omega$ and $12 \Omega$ are connected in parallel. The combination is connected to a 4 V battery with negligible internal resistance. The power dissipated in the $6 \Omega$ resistor is:
questions.s: In a parallel combination, the voltage across each resistor is the same, which is 4 V . Power dissipated in the $6 \Omega$ resistor is $P=\frac{V^{2}}{R}=\frac{4^{2}}{6}=\frac{16}{6}=\frac{8}{3} \approx 2.67$ W.

questions.q: In a meter bridge, the left gap has a resistor of $5 \Omega$ and the right gap has a resistor of $15 \Omega$. The balancing length from the left end is_____ \[\left( {{\text{in}}\,\,\,cm} \right).\]
questions.s: For a balanced bridge, $\frac{R_{L}}{R_{R}}=\frac{l}{100-l} \Rightarrow \frac{5}{15}=\frac{l}{100-l} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{3}=\frac{l}{100-l} \Rightarrow 100-l=3 l \Rightarrow 4 l=100 \Rightarrow l=25 \mathrm{~cm}$.

questions.q: In the half-deflection method for finding galvanometer resistance G , a high resistance R is connected in series with the galvanometer. Then, a shunt S is connected in parallel to the galvanometer to reduce the deflection to half. The galvanometer resistance is given by:
questions.s: In the half-deflection method, for the approximation to be valid (assuming R is very large), the resistance of the galvanometer G is approximately equal to the shunt resistance S that causes the deflection to become half.

questions.q: A wire of resistance $18 \Omega$ is bent in the form of an equilateral triangle. The equivalent resistance across any two vertices of the triangle is \[\left( {{\text{in}}\,\,\Omega } \right).\]
questions.s: The resistance of each side of the triangle is $18 / 3=6 \Omega$. Across any two vertices, one side of $6 \Omega$ is in parallel with the other two sides in series ( $6+6=12 \Omega$ ). $R_{e q}=\frac{6 \times 12}{6+12}=\frac{72}{18}=4 \Omega$.
questions.sub: Calculation of equivalent resistance of a circuit

questions.q: A battery with an EMF of 10 V and an internal resistance of $1 \Omega$ is connected to an external resistor of $4 \Omega$. The power dissipated in the internal resistance of the battery is \[\left( {{\text{in}}\,\,W} \right).\]
questions.s: Total resistance $R_{\text {total }}=R+r=4+1=5 \Omega$. Current in the circuit $I=\frac{E}{R_{\text {total }}}=\frac{10}{5}=2 \mathrm{~A}$. Power dissipated in the internal resistance is $P_{\text {internal }}= I^{2} r=(2)^{2} \times 1=4 \mathrm{~W}$.

questions.q: The resistance of the wire of a meter bridge does not affect the balancing condition because:
o: The wire has a very low resistance.
The wire is uniform and the condition is based on ratios.
The current through the wire is negligible.
The material of the wire is Manganin.
questions.s: The balancing condition is $\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=\frac{\rho l_{1} / A}{\rho l_{2} / A}=\frac{l_{1}}{l_{2}}$. As long as the wire has a uniform cross-section and resistivity, these terms cancel out, and the condition depends only on the ratio of lengths.

questions.q: In an ammeter, $10 \%$ of the main current passes through a galvanometer of resistance $99 \Omega$. The resistance of the shunt is______ \[\left( {{\text{in}}\,\,\,\Omega } \right).\]
questions.s: Current through galvanometer $I_{g}=0.10 I$. Current through shunt $I_{s}=I-I_{g}=I-0.10 I= 0.90 I$. The potential difference is the same across both: $I_{g} G=I_{s} S . \quad(0.10 I) \times 99=(0.90 I) \times S$. $S=\frac{0.10 \times 99}{0.90}=\frac{9.9}{0.9}=11 \Omega$.

questions.q: In an ammeter, $2 \%$ of the main current passes through the galvanometer. If the resistance of the galvanometer is G , the resistance of the shunt is:
questions.s: Current through galvanometer $I_{g}=0.02 I$. Current through shunt $I_{s}=I-I_{g}=0.98 I$. Since the shunt and galvanometer are in parallel, the voltage across them is the same: $I_{g} G=I_{s} S \Rightarrow (0.02 I) G=(0.98 I) S \Rightarrow S=\frac{0.02}{0.98} G=\frac{1}{49} G$.

questions.q:
Two cells with emfs (8V, 2V) and internal resistances (

$1 \Omega$ , 

$2 \Omega$ ) respectively are connected in opposition. The current flowing in the circuit is_________ \[\left( {{\text{in}}\,\,A} \right).\]
questions.s: The cells are in opposition, so the net EMF is $E_{\text {net }}=E_{1}-E_{2}=8-2=6$ V . The total resistance is the sum of the internal resistances, $r_{\text {total }}=r_{1}+r_{2}=1+2= 3 \Omega$. The current in the circuit is $I=\frac{E_{\text {net }}}{r_{\text {total }}}=\frac{6}{3}=2 \mathrm{~A}$.

questions.q: A galvanometer with a coil resistance of $50 \Omega$ shows full-scale deflection for a current of 1 mA . To use it as an ammeter with a range of 1 A , a shunt of resistance S is required. The value of S is________milli-ohms. (rounded to the nearest integer)
questions.s: Using the shunt formula, $S=\frac{I_{g} G}{I-I_{g}}=\frac{\left(1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~A}\right) \times 50 \Omega}{1 \mathrm{~A}-0.001 \mathrm{~A}}=\frac{0.05}{0.999} \approx 0.05005 \Omega$. In milli-ohms, $S=0.05005 \times 1000=50.05 \mathrm{~m} \Omega$. Rounded to the nearest integer, the value is 50 .

questions.q: A voltmeter of resistance $1000 \Omega$ reads 2 V . To make it read 20 V , the extra resistance to be connected in series is:
questions.s: The full-scale deflection current of the original voltmeter is $I_{g}=V / R_{V}=2 / 1000=0.002 \mathrm{~A}$. To increase the range to 20 V , the new total resistance should be $R_{\text {total }}=V_{\text {new }} / I_{g}=20 / 0.002=10000 \Omega$. The extra series resistance needed is $R_{\text {extra }}=R_{\text {total }}-R_{V}=10000-1000=9000 \Omega$.

questions.q: A conducting rod of length $L$ moves with a constant velocity $v$ parallel to its length in a uniform magnetic field $B$ that is perpendicular to the rod. The induced emf between the ends of the rod is:
questions.s: The motional emf is given by $\mathcal{E}=(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \cdot \vec{L}$. Here, $\vec{v}$ is parallel to $\vec{L}$. Therefore, the scalar triple product is zero. Alternatively, the magnetic force on charges is $\vec{F}=q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$, which is perpendicular to the rod's length. Thus, no charge separation occurs along the length of the rod.

questions.q: A generator produces a maximum voltage of 240 V at a frequency of 60 Hz . The number of turns in the coil is 200 and its area is $0.05 \mathrm{~m}^{2}$. The magnitude of the magnetic field in which the coil rotates is approximately:
questions.s: The maximum voltage (peak EMF) is given by $\mathcal{E}_{\text {max }}=N A B \omega$. The angular frequency is $\omega=2 \pi f=2 \pi(60)=120 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} . B=\frac{\mathcal{E}_{\max }}{N A \omega}=\frac{240}{200 \times 0.05 \times 120 \pi}=\frac{240}{10 \times 120 \pi}=\frac{240}{1200 \pi}=\frac{0.2}{\pi} \approx \frac{0.2}{3.14} \approx$ 0.0637 T .

questions.q: In a series RLC circuit connected to a DC source, after the switch has been closed for a long time:
o: Energy stored in the inductor is maximum.
Energy stored in the capacitor is zero.
Energy stored in the inductor is zero and in the capacitor is maximum.
Energy is equally stored in both the inductor and capacitor.
questions.s: In a DC circuit at steady state (after a long time), the inductor acts as a short circuit (wire) and the capacitor acts as an open circuit. Since the capacitor is an open circuit, the current $I$ becomes zero. Therefore, the energy in the inductor ( $U_{L}=\frac{1}{2} L I^{2}$ ) is zero. The capacitor charges to the full battery voltage V , so its stored energy ( $U_{C}=\frac{1}{2} C V^{2}$ ) is maximum.

questions.q: In a Wheatstone bridge, the four arms have resistances $5 \Omega, 10 \Omega, 10 \Omega$, and $20 \Omega$ respectively, and a $15 \Omega$ resistor is connected across the galvanometer terminals. What is the equivalent resistance of the combination?
questions.s: The bridge is arranged such that $P=5, Q=10, R=10, S=20$. The condition $\frac{P}{Q}=\frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{R}{S}=\frac{10}{20}=\frac{1}{2}$ is satisfied. The bridge is balanced. The central $15 \Omega$ resistor can be ignored. The equivalent resistance is the parallel combination of the top arm ( $5+10=15 \Omega$ ) and the bottom arm $(10+20=30 \Omega) . R_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{15 \times 30}{15+30}=\frac{450}{45}=10 \Omega$.

questions.q: A voltmeter of resistance $2000 \Omega$ is used to measure the potential difference across a $200 \Omega$ resistor. The percentage error in the reading is approximately (Assume the current in circuit stays same):
questions.s: The equivalent resistance of the parallel combination is $R_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{200 \times 2000}{200+2000}=\frac{400000}{2200} \approx 181.8 \Omega$. The ratio of measured resistance to true resistance is $\frac{181.8}{200} \approx 0.909$. Since voltage is proportional to resistance (assuming constant current supply), the measured voltage is about $90.9 \%$ of the true voltage. The error is $100-90.9=9.1 \%$, which is approximately $9 \%$.

questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment, a null point is obtained at 60 cm from the left end. If a $3 \Omega$ resistance is connected in series with the smaller of the two resistances, the null point shifts to 50 cm . The values of the two resistances are:
questions.s: Initially, $\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=\frac{60}{40}=\frac{3}{2}$. So $R_{1}=\frac{3}{2} R_{2}$. The smaller resistance is $R_{2}$. After adding $3 \Omega$ to $R_{2}$, the new resistance is $R_{2}+3$. The new null point is $50 \mathrm{~cm} \cdot \frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}+3}=\frac{50}{50}=1 \Rightarrow R_{1}=R_{2}+3$. Substituting the first equation into the second: $\frac{3}{2} R_{2}=R_{2}+3 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} R_{2}=3 \Rightarrow R_{2}=6 \Omega$. Then $R_{1}=\frac{3}{2}(6)=9 \Omega$.

questions.q: In a meter bridge, the balancing length is found to be 25 cm from the left end. If the resistor in the right gap is shunted by an equal resistor, the new balancing point will be:
questions.s: Initially, $\frac{R_{L}}{R_{R}}=\frac{25}{75}=\frac{1}{3}$. So, $R_{R}=3 R_{L}$. When $R_{R}$ is shunted by an equal resistor, the new resistance in the right gap is $R_{R}^{\prime}=\frac{R_{R} \times R_{R}}{R_{R}+R_{R}}=\frac{R_{R}}{2}$. The new balance condition is $\frac{R_{L}}{R_{R}^{\prime}}=\frac{l^{\prime}}{100-l^{\prime}}$. $\frac{R_{L}}{R_{R} / 2}=\frac{2 R_{L}}{3 R_{L}}=\frac{2}{3}=\frac{l^{\prime}}{100-l^{\prime}} \Rightarrow 200-2 l^{\prime}=3 l^{\prime} \Rightarrow 5 l^{\prime}=200 \Rightarrow l^{\prime}=40 \mathrm{~cm}$.

questions.q: A long solenoid having 200 turns per cm carries a current of 1.5 amp . At the centre of it is placed a coil of 100 turns of cross-sectional area $3.14 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2$ having its axis parallel to the field produced by the solenoid. When the direction of current in the solenoid is reversed within 0.05s, the induced emf in the coil is (in milivolts)
questions.s:
The magnetic field inside the solenoid is given by $B=\mu_0 n I$. The initial magnetic flux through the coil is $\Phi_1=N B A$. When the current is reversed, the magnetic field and thus the flux also reverse, becoming $\Phi_2=-N B A$. The change in flux is $\Delta \Phi=\Phi_2-\Phi_1=-2 N B A$. By Faraday's Law, the induced EMF is $\epsilon=\left|\frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t}\right|$.
Using the given values, the induced EMF is calculated to be 0.048 V .

questions.q: A square loop of wire has a total resistance of $4 R$. A battery of emf $\mathcal{E}$ and negligible internal resistance is connected across one side AB . A capacitor $C$ is connected across the diagonal AC. The potential difference across the capacitor is $\mathcal{E} / x$. Find x.
questions.s: Let each side of the square have resistance $R$. Let the vertices be $A, B, C, D$ in order. The battery is across AB . Let the potential at A be 0 and at B be $\mathcal{E}$. The circuit consists of two parallel paths from $A$ to $B$ : the direct side $A B$ (resistance $R$ ), and the path $A D C B$ (resistance $R+R+R =3 \mathrm{R}$ ). This is incorrect. The battery is connected *across* one side. Let's assume the vertices are $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{D}$. Battery across AB . Due to symmetry, the paths ADB and ACB are equivalent if the battery were at the center. With the battery across AB , let's set $V_{A}=0$ and $V_{B}=\mathcal{E}$. The resistance of path ADB is $R+R=2 R$. The resistance of path ACB is $R+R=2 R$. So the current through path ADB is $I_{A D B}=\mathcal{E} /(2 R)$, and the current through ACB is $I_{A C B}=\mathcal{E} /(2 R)$. The potential at D is $V_{D}=V_{A}+I_{A D B} \times R_{A D}=0+\left(\frac{\mathcal{E}}{2 R}\right) \times R=\frac{\mathcal{E}}{2}$. The potential at C is $V_{C}=V_{A}+I_{A C B} \times R_{A C}=0+\left(\frac{\mathcal{E}}{2 R}\right) \times R=\frac{\mathcal{E}}{2}$. This is not correct as C is not adjacent to A in this path. $V_{C}=V_{B}-I_{A C B} \times R_{C B}=\mathcal{E}-\left(\frac{\mathcal{E}}{2 R}\right) \times R=\mathcal{E}-\frac{\mathcal{E}}{2}=\frac{\mathcal{E}}{2}$. The potential difference across the capacitor connected to AC is $\left|V_{C}-V_{A}\right|=\left|\frac{\mathcal{E}}{2}-0\right|=\frac{\mathcal{E}}{2}$. So, the potential difference is $\mathcal{E} / 2$, which means $x=2$.
